classification.difficultyReason: Combine stationary-point zeros with slope signs to sketch derivatives; the hardest case requires recognising that a stationary inflection gives a touching zero without a sign change.

inlines.text: For each of the following graphs of

spec.description: Horizontal function graph at y=1 with arrows at both ends.

answer.worked: The graph of $f$ has gradient $0$ everywhere, so $f'(x)=0$ for every $x$.

spec.description: Increasing straight line crossing the y-axis below the origin.
spec.mathematics: Constant positive gradient; answer key identifies gradient 2.

answer.worked: The straight line has constant gradient $2$, so $f'(x)=2$ at every $x$.

spec.description: Upward parabola symmetric about the y-axis, with vertex below the x-axis.
spec.mathematics: Derivative is negative left of the vertex, zero at x=0 and positive right of it.

answer.short: An increasing straight line through the origin.
answer.worked: The gradient of $f$ increases from negative to positive and is $0$ at its vertex, $x=0$. Hence $f'$ is an increasing line through $(0,0)$.

spec.description: Increasing straight derivative graph through the origin.
spec.mathematics: f'(0)=0, with negative values left and positive values right.

spec.description: Cubic-shaped graph with a local maximum left of the y-axis, a local minimum right of it and a downward crossing at the origin.
spec.mathematics: Derivative zeros at the two turning-point abscissae.

answer.short: An upward parabola crossing the $x$-axis at both turning-point abscissae of $f$, with its vertex below the axis.
answer.worked: At each turning point of $f$, the gradient is $0$. The gradients are positive before the maximum, negative between the turning points and positive after the minimum, giving an upward parabola with two $x$-intercepts.

spec.description: Upward parabola with zeros aligned to the two turning points of the given cubic.
spec.mathematics: Positive, negative, positive derivative sign pattern.

spec.description: Both ends rise; a shallow left minimum, nearby maximum and deeper right minimum.

answer.short: A cubic-shaped graph crossing the $x$-axis at all three turning-point abscissae of $f$; its signs from left to right are $-,+,-,+$.
answer.worked: Mark $f'=0$ beneath each of the three turning points. Reading the slopes of $f$ from left to right gives negative, positive, negative and positive values, so join the zeros with a cubic-shaped curve following those signs.

spec.description: Cubic-shaped derivative with three crossings of the x-axis.
spec.mathematics: Derivative sign pattern negative, positive, negative, positive.

spec.description: Both ends rise; the curve descends through a horizontal flattening at the origin, then reaches a minimum to the right.
spec.mathematics: Stationary inflection at x=0 and later local minimum.

answer.short: A cubic-shaped derivative that touches the $x$-axis at $x=0$, remains negative until the minimum of $f$, then crosses to positive values.
answer.worked: The horizontal flattening at $x=0$ gives $f'(0)=0$, but $f$ decreases on both sides, so $f'$ touches the axis there without crossing. At the later minimum, $f'$ crosses from negative to positive.

spec.description: Derivative touches the x-axis at the origin, dips below it and crosses it at the later minimum's abscissa.
spec.mathematics: f'(0)=0 without a sign change; later zero changes from negative to positive.
